name: Brusquembille
summary: Historical French ace-ten trick-and-draw game with variable trumps and side-payments for aces and tens.
rules_text: Played with 32-card piquet pack, 2-5 players. If 3 or 5 play, remove two Sevens so cards divide evenly. Each player antes to pot and receives 3 cards. Top stock card face-up under stock sets trump and is last card drawn. Eldest leads first trick; any card may be played, no need to follow suit. Highest trump wins trick, otherwise highest of led suit. Trick winner draws first from stock to refill to 3, others follow. Winner leads next. When stock empty, last three tricks require following suit, later rule adds winner of first trick may exchange trump in hand for turned-up trump. After all cards played, count points: Ace 11, Ten 10, King 4, Queen 3, Jack 2, rest 0, plus 1 for a pointless trick in later rules. Most points wins pot. Side-payments: winning a trick containing own Ace gains 2 chips from each opponent, losing own Ace costs 2 chips to each; Ten is 1 chip same way; adjusted for partnerships.
rating_reason: Specific trick-and-draw game, variable trumps, strategic points
